metadata.name: Neurosymbolic Search Composition Router
metadata.purpose: Translate conversational clinical or scientific intent into reproducible, adaptive and evidence-aware PubMed search plans using curated repository filters.

rule_classification.purpose: Every section below belongs to exactly one class. A surface may harden a rule; it must never silently redefine one.
rule_classification.dependency_direction: router -> adapters. A surface that cannot resolve the contract version it requires degrades explicitly instead of improvising.

conformance.how_a_surface_declares_support: State the contract_version implemented, the sections implemented, the repository commit tested and the adapter's own test result. Running this repository suite validates the reference implementation only; it does not certify a third-party adapter.
conformance.reimplementation_allowed: Yes, in any language. Passing the suite is what counts, not sharing code.
conformance.hardening_allowed: A surface may be stricter than this contract.
conformance.silent_redefinition_forbidden: A surface must not loosen or reinterpret a rule without saying so.
conformance.what_the_suite_does_not_prove: It checks contradictions between what is declared and what the repository contains, plus the reference parser against adversarial fixtures. It does not execute or certify code in an external adapter, nor prove that a surface composes a good search, reads evidence well, or applies the principles.

adapter_conformance.rule_vector_completeness: Every rule in query_execution_contract is either a vector in minimum_query_vectors or listed in guiding_prose_not_a_vector. There is no third option: a rule that is neither is a rule no adapter is required to prove. The repository suite enforces this, so adding a rule without its vector fails the suite instead of passing unnoticed.

surface_policy_not_owned_here.rule: These belong to the invoking surface. They are named here so their absence reads as a decision, not an oversight.
items: delegation level and how much the user is asked to do
critical appraisal: effect size, confidence intervals, NNT/NNH, bias, heterogeneity, clinically relevant threshold
how retrieved data, interpretation and hypothesis are kept apart in the answer
the last mile: what any of it changes in practice tomorrow
response language, register, voice or written output, and visual output

principles.statement: Map the overall evidence landscape before privileging or deeply interpreting an individual study.
Never infer the state of the science from an isolated study when broader evidence can reasonably be retrieved.
Continue complementary retrieval passes until additional searches provide little or no clinically meaningful new information, rather than stopping after the first relevant result.
Use broad complementary passes to identify the structure of the evidence, then drill down selectively into studies most likely to change interpretation or practice.

Before repeatedly narrowing one query, explore complementary evidence lanes such as syntheses, primary studies, specialty journals, primary care journals, top general journals, safety signals or trending attention when relevant.
Balance sensitivity and specificity dynamically. Prefer validated filters, but relax or split constraints when filter stacking risks losing important evidence.
Use curated repository filters as the symbolic source of truth whenever an appropriate validated filter exists; do not reconstruct them from memory.
Do not surface a paper as an evidentiary finding without reading at least its abstract or an equivalent primary source.
Prefer current evidence when appropriate, while widening the time horizon for seminal, sparse, rare or historically defining evidence.
Never claim a search, filter, abstract review or source retrieval that was not actually performed.
Do not silently replace literal PubMed retrieval with semantic web search, another academic index or model memory.
Normalize biomedical retrieval concepts to canonical English terminology and MeSH when useful, while responding to the user in the language of the ongoing conversation.

neural.owns: Intent, context, synonyms, MeSH when useful, population, intervention or exposure, outcomes, evidence type, specialty and time frame.
neural.rule: Interprets; never reconstructs a curated filter from memory.

symbolic.rule: Curated repository filters are the symbolic truth. Retrieve them literally or say you did not.

layers.boundary: The router orients; it does not restrict mechanically. If a combination threatens sensitivity, run parallel passes and merge.

pipeline.boundary_rule: Critical appraisal and the last mile belong to the invoking surface. This router does not duplicate them: it delivers retrieval that is real, reproducible and traceable enough for them to stand on.

reading.if_no_abstract: Do not use as a main evidentiary finding unless full text or an equivalent primary source has been read.

exact_applicability_pass.rule: If the landscape pass deliberately dropped a component of the question to protect sensitivity, at least one later pass must put it back before any conclusion is drawn.
exact_applicability_pass.why: Dropping a component is legitimate and often right; never returning to it turns a broad answer into an answer to a different question.
exact_applicability_pass.measured: 2026-09-16: dropping 'metformin' was the right call for the landscape, but the exact question still had 44 records with metformin and 5 with an explicit second-line restriction. None of them were searched for.
exact_applicability_pass.declare: State which component was dropped, in which passes, and what the pass that restored it found.

condition_guideline_pass.rule: For a treatment or management question, the guidelines_or_consensus lane is searched at the level of the condition, without the intervention: a guideline grades interventions that its title and abstract do not name. A guideline lane restricted to the intervention behaves as a replacing_pass (coverage_check) and loses them. It is the landscape side of exact_applicability_pass: the intervention stays in the core and is dropped only here.
condition_guideline_pass.deferred: A lane declared to be covered outside PubMed (guideline bodies, regulators, the web) counts as not run until its result reaches the answer with its source. If it does not, the answer says that the lane was not covered. Deferring it is no reason to skip the PubMed lane for a class that PubMed indexes.
condition_guideline_pass.measured: 2026-10-26, muscle relaxants for acute low back pain: the multidisciplinary guideline of September 2026 (PMID 42687437) recommends them as second line but does not name them in its title or abstract. The core 'low back pain AND muscle relaxants' did not contain it (checked by UID). A guideline pass on acute low back pain without the intervention returned it on its first page. The agent had dropped the guideline filter 'to check guidelines outside PubMed', and that check never reached the answer.
condition_guideline_pass.declare: State the guideline pass and its query, or why the question needs none; for a deferred lane, its source and what it found.

filter_catalog.purpose: What exists and what role each filter plays. The registry names routes; the catalog is how a surface discovers every filter, including those no route mentions. Measured 2026-10-16: GitHub Pages does not list folders, so from a conversational surface a filter outside the registry could not be found at all.
filter_catalog.generated_fields: path, family, title, description, role, registry_key, pair, exclusion, embedded_date_limit, validation, reference, metrics; and for journal lists id, path, name, description, journal_count, role. Everything except role comes from the files themselves.
filter_catalog.freshness_rule: The committed catalog must equal what the generator produces. A new filter without its entry, or a header changed without regenerating, fails the suite (K1).
filter_catalog.role_owner: role_of below is the only hand-declared field. Its meaning lives in composition.roles. A retrieval filter without a role fails the suite (K2).
filter_catalog.family_is_not_role: The folder a filter sits in does not say how to compose it: scope/ holds geography, study designs, domains, a journal list and exclusions; clinical/ holds question types and domains. Compose by role, never by folder or key name.

filter_file_contract.structure: Header lines starting with #, then the query (one or more lines), then a line exactly equal to @@@FILTER_METADATA@@@, then a JSON validation block.
extraction: Split the file at the first line exactly equal to @@@FILTER_METADATA@@@.
In the part before, drop empty lines and lines starting with #.
Join ALL remaining lines with a single space, preserving parentheses and operators.
Never take only the first non-comment line: multi-line filters would be truncated into a plausible but wrong query.
filter_file_contract.false_zero_warning: If the metadata block is swallowed into the query, PubMed returns count 0 with the error hidden in errorlist.phrasesnotfound and quotedphrasesnotfound empty.
filter_file_contract.modified_filter_declaration: Modifying a filter is legitimate but must be declared as {path, modified: true, reason, effective_query}, and it is the effective_query that provenance refers to.

fidelity_check.rule: An engine that holds the catalog can check that every filter the surface declares as used appears literally in the sent query, whitespace aside, and that no exclusion filter follows an AND. The result is filter_fidelity: verified when all are present and correctly composed, failed otherwise. A modified filter is not declared as used; it is declared under modified_filter_declaration.
fidelity_check.why: validated_filters_as_symbolic_truth was a rule no conversational surface could prove: a filter rebuilt from memory, or truncated to its first line, produces a plausible query and a verified integrity status. Integrity says PubMed ran what was sent; fidelity says what was sent contains the curated filter.
fidelity_check.reference: filterFidelity() in mcp/protocol.mjs; served by the MCP together with pubmed_filter_catalog and pubmed_get_filter (canonical extraction by the reference parser).

query_execution_contract.rule: Every executed query is inspected before its result is used. PubMed already reports what it ignored; the failure is not reading it.
query_execution_contract.mesh_terms_are_not_exempt: A MeSH heading invented by a model is medically plausible and syntactically valid, so it raises no error: PubMed simply drops it and reports it under quotedphrasesnotfound. Measured 2026-09-16: '"Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease"[Mesh]' returns 0 records with no errorlist. Inside an OR block it cost nothing; as an AND block it would have returned zero for the whole search. The official descriptor is 'Atherosclerosis'.
query_execution_contract.rule_for_headings: db=mesh is useful for discovery, but a returned entry term can map to a different descriptor and therefore does not prove literal identity. Any [Mesh] or [mh] heading must be validated by executing the exact tagged heading in db=pubmed with retmax=0, requiring a non-empty querytranslation and confirming that it is absent from quotedphrasesnotfound and phrasesignored. A heading that was dropped is reported, never presented as if it had contributed.
query_execution_contract.zero_is_not_always_zero: count 0 with a non-empty quotedphrasesnotfound is a broken query, not an empty field.
query_execution_contract.translation_check: Read querytranslation to confirm PubMed parsed what was intended, particularly around NOT clauses, phrase matching and automatic term mapping.
query_execution_contract.count_must_be_a_count: A missing, empty or non-numeric count is not a count. A response without a usable count cannot be reported as "N records found", whatever else it carries. The usual way this breaks is coercion in the adapter, not PubMed: parseInt(count) || 0 turns an absent or malformed count into a plausible zero, and parseInt accepts a numeric prefix, so '12abc' becomes 12. Found 2026-09-29 by static audit of a public PubMed MCP server.
query_execution_contract.dropped_term_with_results: A dropped term is most dangerous when the query still returns results: no zero, no error, a plausible count. Measured 2026-09: PubMed dropped "body battery"[tiab] from an OR block and returned 5 records, the same 5 the query without that term returns. Absence of a zero is not evidence of integrity.
query_execution_contract.diagnostics_come_from_the_response: querytranslation, warninglist, errorlist and ERROR are read from PubMed's own response (retmode=xml carries the same as QueryTranslation, WarningList, ErrorList and ERROR). Nothing a tool builds itself substitutes for them: an echo of the query it sent (effective, sanitized or normalized query) shows what was sent, not what PubMed executed; a list of filters it applied shows what it asked for, not what PubMed kept; a prose notice that summarises some warning types proves nothing about the types it never checks, so the absence of a notice is not the absence of a warning. An engine that does not return these fields produces a pass that was executed but is not verifiable. Found 2026-09-29 by static audit of a public PubMed MCP server: querytranslation was parsed internally and never returned, and neither phrasesignored nor outputmessages reached the consumer, which received the sent query labelled as effective query and a notice covering three warning types.
query_execution_contract.transport_carries_the_whole_query: A composed query travels in the request body (POST, application/x-www-form-urlencoded), or the engine is shown to switch to POST before URL limits. A topic plus an inline methodological filter routinely exceeds what a GET URL carries. Measured 2026-09-28: E-utilities accepted a GET of 3,573 URL-encoded characters and answered HTTP 414 at 5,343; one conversational engine answered 414 at 2,925 characters of query. A rejected or truncated request is a declared transport failure: never a zero, never 'no results', never 'not evaluable', and never silently retried with a shortened query. An engine whose transport is unknown is tested with a query above those lengths before it runs composed filters.
query_execution_contract.field_tags_are_not_reported: PubMed reports nothing when it ignores a field tag, so the response alone cannot reveal it; the check is made on the sent query. Measured 2026-10-08 against E-utilities, all with clean diagnostics and a plausible count: an unknown tag ('asthma[foo]', the typo 'asthma[tiabb]', also with a space before it: tags apply across whitespace); a tag on a group with AND, OR or NOT ('(asthma OR copd)[tiab]' searches all fields: 351,416 against 257,958 for asthma[tiab] OR copd[tiab]); a modifier on a field that does not take it (':~N' only on title, title/abstract and affiliation; ':noexp' only on MeSH, subheading and publication type: 'asthma[mh:~3]' runs as plain MeSH); proximity not applied to a quoted phrase of two or more words without wildcards ('"asthma* control"[tiab:~2]' and 'asthma control[tiab:~2]' drop the proximity); and a look-alike truncation character, also inside a quoted phrase ('intervent∗[ti]' with U+2217 = 9 records, 'intervent*[ti]' = 269,566; '"randomized trial∗"[tiab]' = 65,068 against 109,950). Brackets inside a quoted phrase are text, not tags ('"[18F]FDG"[tiab]' is valid). Any of these makes the pass failed. A judgement made without the sent query cannot be verified. Reference: fieldTagIssues() and lookalikeCharacters() in scripts/parse-filter.mjs, PUBMED_FIELD_TAGS verified tag by tag.
query_execution_contract.pagination_window: A page PubMed rejects is never a count, and fewer records retrieved than counted is declared, never presented as all of them. The size of the window is an observed, dated limit, not part of this rule: on 2026-10-08 PubMed ESearch served the first 9,999 records (retstart <= 9998) and said so in its own ERROR, against the 10,000 in NCBI's documentation. Beyond it the ERROR arrives as malformed JSON (a raw newline inside the string), and an adapter that cannot read it and falls back to 0 fabricates a zero, as one conversational connector did for asthma[tiab]. A request overlapping the edge is trimmed with outputmessages 'Restrictions achieved...': a pagination notice, not a query-integrity warning. The reference executor trims such a request before sending it and records both sizes (request.retmax_requested and request.retmax_sent). A receipt says whether there is a next page and, when there is none, why (next_retstart_reason: not_verified, count_only, page_adjusted, empty_page, end_of_set, window_limit); no next page never means that everything was retrieved.

registry_validation.rule: validated_filters_as_symbolic_truth applies to filters carrying a published validation reference. The entries listed below are author-made and have none; cite them as such and never present them as validated.
registry_validation.journal_lists_bias: Journal lists are derived from h5-index rankings; restricting by them narrows by prestige, not by method.
registry_validation.sensitive_specific_pair_not_always_avail: Only 12 repository filters have both versions. clinical.drug_adverse_events has no specific variant; do not improvise one.
registry_validation.registry_is_a_subset: The registry covers 31 of the 48 retrieval filters in the repository: it names the routes this router knows by question type. The catalog (filter_catalog.path) lists all 48 and every journal list, with what each one is for and its default role. Read the catalog, not the registry, to decide whether a filter exists for a facet of the question.

terms_pubmed_drops.rule: Curated filters are the source of methodological intent, not an authority on today's PubMed syntax. A term inside a validated filter can still be dropped by the engine.
terms_pubmed_drops.swept: 122 filters (48 retrieval filters and the journal lists) executed against E-utilities with scripts/sweep-filters.mjs on 2026-10-16: 118 clean; 4 journal lists carry abbreviations of journals PubMed does not index, accepted in scripts/sweep-baseline.json. No retrieval filter has a term PubMed drops.

benign.what: A quoted free-text phrase that simply does not occur in the literature. The syntax is fine and the filter works; PubMed only says the phrase matched nothing.

dead_field_tags.what: A term addressed to a field where it does not exist. It contributes nothing and looks as if it did.

terms_pubmed_drops.declaration_rule: Every term listed under benign.cases or dead_field_tags.cases is written literally as it appears in the filter, and the suite fails if the filter no longer contains it. A declaration that outlives its defect describes a repository that no longer exists (R18).

resolved.2026-10-01: Four filters had terms PubMed dropped, found on 2026-09-16: two benign phrases in filters/methodology/clinical_rules_ap.txt, "network meta-analysis"[mh] in filters/methodology/indirect_comparison.txt (not a MeSH descriptor; +0.02% as [pt]) and two consensus terms in filters/methodology/gpc.txt and filters/scope/pearls.txt. Revived or replaced by the owner in commit a7bd7c8. This section kept describing them until 2026-10-16, when an audit noticed; R18 makes that impossible now.

terms_pubmed_drops.how_this_was_found: By applying the router's own query_execution_contract to the repository's own filters. The rule written for a model's invented MeSH heading found four cases inside curated filters.

typographic_truncation.what: A character that looks like the truncation asterisk but is not one, usually copied from a PDF. PubMed searches the bare stem and reports nothing, so no sweep sees it.

resolved.filters/methodology/horizon.txt: Six terms carried U+2217 instead of * (emergente, intervent, surger, tool, transplant and, in the exclusion block, VACCIN). Measured 2026-10-08: 356,107 records as written against 420,561 corrected (+18%). Corrected by the owner on 2026-10-09 as V.1.2, after checking the source article's Table 1, which prints every asterisk with that glyph, including obvious truncations.

typographic_truncation.completeness_rule: Every filter carrying such a character must be listed here. The suite fails otherwise (R17), and also fails if a listed filter no longer has it, so a correction removes the entry.

composition.topic_plus_scope_filter: AND only when the scope DEFINES the population the question is about (scope_roles.population_defining). When it only conditions applicability, it is a parallel lane (scope_roles.applicability). The wording 'part of the question' was ambiguous enough to justify an AND that was measured to lose most of the evidence.

roles.rule: Every filter in the catalog has one default role (filter_catalog.role_of). The role says how the filter enters a search by default; the question can override it (facet_roles), and the override is recorded in provenance.selection_record.

concept.means: Encodes a concept of the question (deprescribing, palliative care, generative AI, CAR-T, simulation, patient safety, evidence-based practice as a topic).
concept.how: OR it inside the block of that concept, together with the agent's own vocabulary for the same concept (within_same_concept). Do not stack it as an extra AND layer on top of terms that already express the concept.
concept.measured: 2026-10-16, deprescribing benzodiazepines in older people, retention of 24 cited studies: the deprescription filter alone 22, the agent's own deprescribing terms 22, both ORed 23.

question_type.means: Clinical question type (therapy, diagnosis, prognosis, etiology, predictors, prediction rules, diagnostic value of a sign or manoeuvre), mostly Haynes hedges with sensitive and specific versions. The clinical examination filter is a diagnostic hedge: AND it with the disease and the sign, never OR it with the sign, or its diagnostic terms replace the sign (Shaikh 2011).
question_type.how: AND with the topic. A specific version that replaces the core is subject to coverage_check.unit: if it loses eligible pearls, fall back (adaptation.if_pearls_lost).

design.means: Type of evidence or publication (syntheses, guidelines, qualitative, indirect comparison, economic evaluation, patient knowledge, views and values, horizon scanning).
design.how: One lane per design, ANDed within its lane; lanes run in parallel and are merged by PMID.

harm.means: Adverse effects of drugs, devices or procedures.
harm.how: Its own lane. Harm evidence is largely observational: do not route it through a therapy filter tuned to trials (routing.safety).

outcome.means: A specific outcome or effect measure (mortality, NNT/NNH). Both are author-made.
outcome.how: AND only in a precision lane when that outcome is what is asked; never restricts the core.

population_setting.means: Age group, care setting or geography (geriatrics, pediatrics, primary care, Spain).
population_setting.how: A parallel lane by default. AND only when it defines the population (scope_roles.population_defining).

editorial.means: Journal lists and editorial formats (jnl_* lists, nursing journals, clinical pearls). Not validated retrieval filters.
editorial.how: Parallel enrichment lane; never a restriction of the core (journal_filters_default_role).

exclusion.means: A filter whose query starts with NOT.
exclusion.how: Appended with NOT, never AND (negation_filters). The suite checks that this role and a leading NOT always coincide (K3).

facet_roles.rule: The neural layer splits the question into facets (concepts, question type, population, setting, place, time, wanted evidence) and gives each one a role IN THIS QUESTION. The catalog role is the default; the question decides.
facet_roles.core: AND. Defines what is being asked; dropping it answers a different question.
facet_roles.concept: OR within its block (agent vocabulary plus any concept filter).
facet_roles.lane: A parallel pass merged by PMID: evidence types, applicability, editorial enrichment.
facet_roles.context: Not a search constraint: who asks or from where (primary_care_policy.user_context_is_not_a_search_constraint).
facet_roles.interpretation: Looked at when reading, not when searching.

population_defining.rule: The question is about that population or setting: AND.
population_defining.example: 'Prevalence of clarithromycin resistance in Spanish patients': Spain is core.

applicability.rule: The question is about an effect or a practice and the scope is where the answer will be used: keep the core free of it and run a parallel applicability lane. That lane may need its own sub-question, often not the core's.
applicability.example: 'Rescue therapy for H. pylori in Spain': efficacy comes from international trials (core, no geography); what Spain changes is local resistance, so the applicability lane asks about resistance AND Spain.
applicability.measured: 2026-10-16: core 26 of 26 cited rescue trials; core AND filters/scope/spanish.txt 2 of 26. The applicability lane on local resistance (2021-2026) returned 53 records, 38 of them outside the core.

scope_roles.user_context: Who asks is context, not scope (primary_care_policy). Measured 2026-10-16 on SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure, 5 included trials: core 5 of 5; AND primary care specific 0; AND primary care journals 0; AND geriatrics 0.

geographic_filters.rule: A geographic filter is a broad signal built on affiliations and mentions of places, not a guarantee that the study population is from there. Confirm population and setting in each article before using it as local evidence.
geographic_filters.measured: 2026-10-16, filters/scope/spanish.txt on H. pylori resistance: the lane brought Spanish surveillance studies and also studies from Chile, Bangladesh, Ireland and Slovenia with a Spanish affiliation or a European registry led from Spain.
geographic_filters.date_windows: Declare a window exactly: '2021:2026[dp]' is six calendar years and can include dates after the search; a rolling five years is a different query. A publication date is not the date the data were collected.

catalog_check.rule: Every facet of the question is checked against the catalog (filter_catalog). A filter whose purpose matches a facet and is not used needs a reason in provenance.selection_record. This obliges consideration, never use.
catalog_check.replaces: Per-dimension activation lists (geography, deprescribing, palliative care, economics...). One general rule covers every facet and every future filter; a list would cover only the dimensions someone remembered.
catalog_check.why: Discovery was pull: a filter was considered only if the agent already suspected it existed, and on conversational surfaces it could not be found at all.

composition.journal_filters_default_role: parallel editorial enrichment passes, not mandatory restriction of the core search
composition.same_family_filters: Do not AND sensitive and specific versions of the same filter; choose one or run separate passes.
composition.overconstraint_rule: If stacking filters threatens sensitivity, split into parallel searches and merge later.
composition.topic_building: Use MeSH and title/abstract synonyms when useful without forcing every PICO component into the query.

indexing_status_is_not_mesh.rule: Status=MEDLINE does not imply MeSH. From the PubMed 2027 baseline (December 2026), citations in scope for MEDLINE but without an abstract move from In Process to MEDLINE with IndexingMethod="NotIndexed" and carry no MeSH. A concept reached only through [mh], or a status subset (medline[sb], inprocess[sb], pubmednotmedline[sb], publisher[sb]) used as a proxy for indexing, silently misses them.
indexing_status_is_not_mesh.when_sensitivity_matters: Pair MeSH with title/abstract terms for the same concept. Depending on MeSH alone is legitimate when deliberate; then declare it in the pass.
indexing_status_is_not_mesh.not_a_reason_to_drop_mesh: The change relabels status; it removes MeSH from no record that had it.
indexing_status_is_not_mesh.repository_check: No filter in the repository uses a status subset. The suite fails if one starts to without being listed in declared_status_subset_filters.

negation_filters.rule: A filter whose query starts with NOT is an exclusion clause and must be appended WITHOUT AND: write `(topic) NOT (...)`, never `(topic) AND (NOT ...)`.
negation_filters.why: PubMed parses `AND (NOT X)` as `AND X`, silently inverting the filter and returning exactly what it was meant to exclude.
negation_filters.measured: 2026-09-15, E-utilities: `(metformin[tiab])` = 36016; `(metformin[tiab]) AND (scope.humans)` = 5852, animal studies only, with NOT dropped in querytranslation; `(metformin[tiab]) NOT (scope.humans)` = 30164. The wrong count is plausible and is not detectable by inspection.
negation_filters.detect_before_composing: Read the filter query first; if it starts with NOT, use NOT composition.
negation_filters.completeness_rule: Every filter in the repository whose query starts with NOT must appear either in affected_registry_entries or here. The suite fails otherwise, so a new exclusion filter cannot be added unnoticed.

embedded_date_limits.rule: Before applying a filter, check whether its own query embeds a date restriction; if it does, it silently overrides the date policy of this router.
embedded_date_limits.removal_is_restructuring: Deleting only the date term can leave `AND ( NOT Y)`, which is the inversion described in negation_filters. Restructure instead, and declare the modified query.
embedded_date_limits.completeness_rule: Every filter in the repository that embeds a date restriction must be listed here. The suite fails otherwise.

why_each_one.filters/scope/pearls.txt: Carries "last 5 years"[dp] inside the filter, in a position where deleting the date term alone inverts the filter. Restructure, do not delete.
why_each_one.filters/scope/ai_especifico.txt: Carries an explicit ("2022/01/01"[PDAT] : "2090/12/31"[PDAT]) window, deliberate for large language model literature. Legitimate, but it silently overrides any wider date policy: say so when the question is declared sparse or historical.

precision_hints.what_they_are: Terms added only to raise precision, not part of the question: versus, vs, comparative, head-to-head, active comparator, and similar.
precision_hints.rule: They are marked as precision hints and REMOVED when falling back from a specific filter to a sensitive one. Swapping the methodological filter while keeping them does not widen the search; it only looks like it did.
precision_hints.measured: 2026-09-16, a real GLP-1 vs SGLT2 question: topic alone 334 records; topic with precision hints 115; with Therapy/Narrow 10; with Therapy/Broad keeping the hints 95; with Therapy/Broad after dropping them 237. The fallback recovered 95 of the 237 it could have reached.
precision_hints.distinguish_from: core_concept terms, which belong to the question and are never dropped.

background.then: Add primary studies when syntheses are old, incomplete, conflicting or insufficient.

treatment.rct_lane: Use a dedicated validated RCT filter when available and direct randomized evidence is required.

safety.means: Harm from a drug, device or procedure: adverse events, toxicity, rare or late harms. Most of this evidence is observational; a therapy filter tuned to trials loses it (measured 2026-10-16: 0 of 18 cited observational studies on fluoroquinolones and aortic aneurysm with Therapy/Narrow, 18 of 18 with clinical.drug_adverse_events).
safety.devices_and_procedures: clinical.device_adverse_events for devices; filters/clinical/surgery_ae.txt for surgical procedures (see the catalog).
safety.not_this: scope.safety_specific and scope.safety_sensitive are PATIENT SAFETY filters (medical errors, safety management; Tanon 2010), not drug safety. They belong to routing.patient_safety. Until 1.10 they sat in this route because of their key name; on a drug question they returned 1 record and 0 of 18 reference studies.

patient_safety.means: Safety of care: medical errors, adverse events of care, safety management, incident reporting.

trending.if_user_says_last_week: Run two lanes: trending without a date restriction and publications from the requested recent window.
trending.what_is_known: PubMed translates trending[sb] to "trending"[Filter]. NCBI does not document the algorithm; library guides describe it as records with a recent rise in PubMed views against a baseline of about a week. Treat any finer claim about how it ranks as unknown.
trending.journal_list_intersection: trending[sb] AND a journal list is a separate lane, never the core: with a small specialty or primary care list it can leave almost nothing.
trending.measured: 2026-10-19, ESearch: trending[sb] = 1165. Of those, 336 (29%) were published more than 30 days earlier and 53 carry a future publication date (issues not yet out). trending[sb] AND 2026/10/13:2026/10/19[dp] = 133; with "last 7 days"[dp] = 264, because the relative form runs to 3000/01/01 and keeps future-dated issues. AND a journal list: jnl_top_publications 107, jnl_cardiology 27, jnl_rheumatology 5, jnl_primary_health_care 1.
trending.web_vs_api: The PubMed web interface and ESearch compute trending[sb] from different sets, so an ESearch count (every number in 'measured', and any receipt) is not the count a user sees on opening the same query in PubMed. 2026-10-19, same query, ESearch vs web: trending[sb] 1167 vs 1000 (the web caps at 1000); diabetes AND trending[sb] 85 vs 70, only 14 PMIDs in common; cancer AND trending[sb] 344 vs 278; trending[sb] AND "last 7 days"[dp] 270 vs 573. Stable over repeated calls. Without trending[sb] both return identical counts. Report trending counts as approximate and never claim the web will show the same records.

corpus_definition.use_when: The product describes or analyses a defined population of records (bibliometrics, production or collaboration mapping, evidence-map counts, an inventory for management or teaching) rather than answering a clinical question.
corpus_definition.population: Declared before analysis: query, period with its date field, document types, languages and eligibility. The query defines what can enter; eligibility decides what stays.
corpus_definition.adaptation: not_applicable: narrowing with methodology, journal or date filters to make results readable changes the population. If narrowing is needed, it is an amendment recorded with date, reason and whether results were already known.
corpus_definition.saturation_policy: not_applicable: the declared population is retrieved completely. records_retrieved equals result_count, or every date tranche does.
corpus_definition.screening: Every excluded record keeps its PMID, reason and reading level (title, abstract or full text). A record that cannot be decided stays unclear; it is never excluded silently.
corpus_definition.external_index_search: A thematic search in another index is a discovery lane. Its records enter only through a recorded corpus revision; they never enrich the existing corpus.
corpus_definition.enrichment: By identifier (PMID, DOI). Provider, date and match status per record. A missing value is not zero, and counts from different providers are neither mixed nor averaged.
corpus_definition.scope_statement: Results describe the PubMed subset reached by the declared query. Claims about a multidisciplinary field as a whole need other indexes.

primary_care_policy.rule: The specialty or setting of the person asking is not by itself a search constraint: it does not justify restricting every search to that setting.
primary_care_policy.use_primary_scope_filter_when: The setting, population, service model or question itself is specifically about primary care.
primary_care_policy.journal_name_is_not_scope: Do not equate relevance to primary care with journals carrying 'primary care' in their title.

reading_and_drilldown.drill_down_decision_owner: The invoking surface decides which findings deserve a drill-down. This router only states how to reach the sources and that an abstract is the minimum before surfacing a paper.

reading_path.rule: Each pass declares how it will be read, before its results, in provenance.selection_record (passes[].reading_path). It is a declaration of intent: it does not certify that anything was read, nor that the selection was good.
reading_path.complete_retrieval: Intent to retrieve every PMID of the defined set, for a screening or a map that needs it. It is reported as completed only after the page controls of pagination pass, and then with their limited guarantee. A count does not need it: a verified result_count is enough to say how many records there are. Retrieving every PMID does not prove that every abstract was read.
reading_path.focused_selection: States which records will be read and why they can support the claim (selection_reason). It may be a pass retrieved whole or a partial selection whose truncation, criterion and limits are stated. coverage_check applies where it would. Sorting by relevance does not show that the selection is adequate or representative.
reading_path.exploration_only: To see the size and shape of a set and plan the next pass. Never counted as a read corpus. Reading records from that batch afterwards is documented as a separate step, not attributed to the earlier record.

reading_and_drilldown.ordered_sample_is_not_the_set: The first N records of a truncated list, in any order, do not represent the set. They feed reading only inside a declared focused_selection with its reason, or as one page of a complete_retrieval. No sort is required: when a pass is retrieved whole the order does not change coverage, and keeping the default order of a partial list can be a deliberate choice. Measured 2026-10-17/18: ESearch returns the most recent entries first by default, and the trials that answered three of five behaviour-test questions were outside the lists the agent read; sort relevance put 5/5 within the first 150 in J and 0/11 within the first 30 in A2, so it is an option, not a guarantee.

order_hides_by_age.rule: Each order can leave important evidence out of a truncated head. The default order sorts by entry date, which is not necessarily the publication date, so older pivotal records sink; relevance (Best Match) combines term matching with a learned re-ranking, gives some extra weight to recently published articles, and can still push a recent record down, as measured below. These are observed risks, not a causal law of age. A focused_selection that truncates a pass states which order it took, its limit and how the selection was made.
order_hides_by_age.when_both_matter: When the claim needs the pivotal evidence and also whatever may have replaced it (a treatment question resting on a synthesis or a guideline), read the head of the same query in both orders, or retrieve the whole list when it fits in one call and screen it. Same sent_query in both calls, not a different query.
order_hides_by_age.cost: A search receipt carries PMIDs, not titles. Screening a whole list by title takes at least one call per 50 PMIDs, more if some stay pending (title_screen, pubmed_summary_exact in the repository MCP); turning a screened record into a finding still means reading it, declared as reading. The cost is in reading, not in retrieving.
order_hides_by_age.measured: 2026-10-26, muscle relaxants for acute low back pain: a synthesis pass of 59 records was read at retmax 15 by relevance. A systematic review published a month earlier (PMID 42799684), inside that pass and able to change the conclusion, sat 17th by relevance and 1st by default order. A guideline of the same month sat 47th of 729 by relevance and 10th by default in a guideline pass. The 2021 review that anchored the answer was within the first 10 in both orders.
order_hides_by_age.not_a_rule_for: It does not make the default order better than relevance, nor ask for both heads on every pass: a pass retrieved whole, or a claim that does not depend on what is current, does not need it.

title_screen.rule: A title screen decides what to read and what to set aside as not pertinent, and is declared as a title screen (coverage_check: state whether relevance was judged on titles or abstracts). It never turns a record into a finding nor highlights it: that still needs the record read (abstract or full text), as defaults.reading requires. title_only_selection_forbidden governs what is reported, not what is read.
title_screen.counted_apart: Records set aside on title are counted apart, as titles screened: never as read and discarded, never as abstracts obtained.
title_screen.tool: With the repository MCP, pubmed_summary_exact returns title, year, publication types, journal, DOIs and NCBI's has-abstract flag for up to 50 PMIDs per call, with a receipt (counts_as: titles_screened). A record that does not fit goes to pending_pmids, never cut. Then read what was kept with pubmed_fetch_exact.
title_screen.does_not_certify: That a title was read or understood; that what was set aside is not pertinent (the agent's judgement, declared); that the summary matches the EFetch record field by field; or any coverage: screening a list does not widen the search that produced it.

pagination.order_recommendation: For a multi-page complete_retrieval, prefer omitting sort rather than using relevance. Identical relevance requests have returned different ordered lists. This precaution does not freeze the default order or the set: keep the drift controls and the no-snapshot limit. When one call returns the whole set, order does not change membership coverage.
pagination.rule: Pages are independent calls with retstart (and the same sort). The server keeps nothing, so a set of pages carries no snapshot guarantee: each page proves the integrity of its query, its list and the position requested, not that the set stayed the same between pages.
drift_controls: same sent_query_sha256 and same request.sort on every page
first page at retstart 0 and each page starting where the previous one ended
every page complete for its stretch: n = min(retmax_sent, max(0, result_count - retstart))
no PMID repeated across pages, and the union equal to result_count when the set fits in the window
pagination.grouping: Pages are joined by the walk they belong to (plan_ref and pass_id of the selection record), never just because their parameters coincide.
pagination.label: When the controls pass the union is reported as an operational retrieval without a fixed snapshot, never as a certified exhaustive set. When any fails it is incomplete, and said so.
pagination.known_limit: The controls cannot detect a set that changed between pages while keeping its count: A, B, C, D becoming A, C, D, E between page 1 (A, B) and page 2 (D, E) loses C with every control passing. A product that needs a fixed, reproducible set (a map or a publishable screening) uses the NCBI history server, outside this contract version, or declares this limit.

saturation_policy.recency_before_closing: recent_evidence_may_change_older_syntheses is checked, not assumed. Before closing on a synthesis or a guideline, look for a newer one of the same class for the question, in the default-order head of the synthesis and guideline passes (reading_and_drilldown.order_hides_by_age), and report what was found or that nothing newer appeared. Newer does not outrank older by date alone: compare population, comparators, included trials and outcomes.
saturation_policy.not_applicable_to: routing.corpus_definition, which needs complete retrieval of a declared population, not conceptual saturation.

coverage_check.purpose: query_integrity verified says the query ran as written. It says nothing about whether the query reaches what the question needs. This section is how the coverage dimension gets a value.
required_when: a report, review, decision or publication rests on the result set
a count, a trend or an absence of evidence is reported
coverage_check.optional_when: Quick orientation answers that claim nothing about how much exists. Say that coverage was not checked.
coverage_check.unit: What is checked is a claim together with the query or union of passes that supports it, not each pass on its own. Wherever this section says 'main query', it means that unit. A synthesis lane need not retrieve a trial, and an applicability lane need not retrieve international trials; demanding it would force fallbacks for omissions that were expected.
coverage_check.eligible_pearls: Pearls are eligible for the purpose of the unit they test: a trial for an efficacy claim, an observational study for a harm claim, a national study for a local-applicability claim. Citations in a review are not its included studies; take pearls from the included studies, a guideline's evidence table or the user, and record their source.
coverage_check.replacing_pass: A pass that replaces the core instead of running beside it (a specific version where the topic or the sensitive version would have run) is checked against the core's eligible pearls before anything rests on it. If it loses eligible pearls that no other pass of the unit recovers (compensation), adaptation.if_pearls_lost applies; a loss compensated within the unit is recorded, not reacted to. A large result count is not evidence of coverage.
coverage_check.compensation: If another pass in the same unit recovers what one pass lost, record which pass compensated: the unit is then the union, and the loss is not a coverage failure.

method.sensitivity_minus_main: Build a broader query (synonyms, spelling variants, wider field tags, the vocabulary of earlier periods), run it NOT the main query, and screen what comes back. Report how many records outside are relevant, with their PMIDs.
method.independent_pearls: 2 to 4 records known to be relevant that did not come from the main results (a guideline, a reference list, a citation supplied by the user, a lateral search with different vocabulary). Check each with (<main query>) AND <PMID>[pmid] at retmax 0. A pearl drawn from the main results approves the query it is meant to test and does not count.
method.same_issue_signal: Missed records published next to included ones (same special issue, adjacent PMIDs) are strong evidence of a lexical gap.
method.field_check: A title-only strategy for a corpus says why, and reports the count of its [tiab] variant.

coverage_check.status: Recorded in provenance.operational_status under the coverage dimension. verified: the check ran and found no relevant records outside, or only isolated ones that cannot change the product (they are listed anyway); it does not mean nothing is missing. failed: it found relevant records outside in a number or of a kind that can change counts, trends or conclusions (a share of the set, a period, a core record). unsupported: it could not run (no literal engine, no independent pearls). planned: not run yet.
coverage_check.on_failed: Revise the query and run it again, or narrow the declared scope explicitly so that the missed records fall outside it. Counts, trends or shares from a corpus whose coverage is failed are never reported without saying so next to the numbers.
coverage_check.screening_basis: Relevance of the records outside is the agent's judgement. State whether it was made on titles or abstracts.
coverage_check.measured: 2026-10-14: a title-only bibliometric query on artificial consciousness returned query_integrity verified with 115 records, 77 kept. Its sensitivity query minus the main one returned 183 records, 34 of them relevant by title, so at least 31% of the relevant set was missing. The query had the phrase "machine consciousness" but not machines or robots, and it caught the clinical sense of conscious. For 2017-2022 it kept 4 records and missed 18, so the reported trend was an artefact of vocabulary. Several missed records were published in the same issues as included ones.

selection_record.purpose: Makes the choice of filters auditable: what the question was split into, what was considered, what was used and what was left out, and why. Integrity says a query ran as written; this says why it was the query.

fields.catalog_ref: contract_version plus catalog_sha256. It stands for 'available'; the catalog is not copied into every run.
fields.filters: [{path, decision: used | discarded, pass_id, role_used, reason}]. Every catalog filter whose purpose matches a facet appears here (composition.catalog_check). role_used differs from the catalog role only with a reason.
fields.passes: [{pass_id, purpose, unit_claim, reading_path, selection_reason}]: what each pass is for, which claim it supports (coverage_check.unit) and how it will be read (reading_and_drilldown.reading_path: complete_retrieval | focused_selection | exploration_only). selection_reason is required with focused_selection.
fields.date_window: {limit, origin: user | agent_policy | filter | none, unrestricted_pass_id, reason} for every pass with a date limit. An agent_policy window names the pass that runs the same core without it (adaptation.date_window_check).
fields.known_pmids: [{pmid, origin: search_pass | cited_in_document | user | model_prior_knowledge | undetermined, detail}] for every PMID fetched by identifier rather than taken from a returned list. undetermined is a valid answer; inventing a source is not. A PMID fetched by identifier feeds reading_and_drilldown, never coverage (tool_requirements.identifier_retrieval).

selection_record.record_at_decision_time: Written when the plan is made and updated when it changes, like every other counter. A selection explained after the results are known is a justification, not a record.
selection_record.on_the_repository_mcp: Sent as the selection_record argument of pubmed_search_exact, one per pass. The receipt echoes it with the server time at which it arrived, taken before PubMed is queried, its SHA-256, and a mechanical check against the catalog and filters_used (status.selection_record: declared | inconsistent | not_declared). It proves the record existed before that run, not before any earlier search in the conversation, and it is the agent's declaration: never part of query_integrity or filter_fidelity. For an agent_policy date window it checks that another pass id was declared, not that the pass ran or was compared; an origin user window cannot be checked by the server. A focused_selection without selection_reason is inconsistent; a pass without reading_path stays declared, with a note in selection_record.notes kept apart from problems. The record is never checked against the page: a partial first page does not contradict a complete_retrieval. The server stores nothing.
selection_record.why_on_the_tool: Measured 2026-10-17/18 (ChatGPT behaviour test, five questions): the selection record was written after the results in five of five runs, although the surface instructions asked for it before. An instruction alone did not produce it; a field the receipt checks makes its absence visible.
selection_record.not_a_judgement: Recording an applicability lane says which passes were run. Judging whether the evidence applies stays with the surface (surface_policy_not_owned_here); that is why operational_status has no applicability dimension.

provenance.no_memory_completion: Do not complete from model memory a concrete datum that should have come from the source. If it was not retrieved, say so.
provenance.counts_are_not_interchangeable: result_count is what PubMed reports; records_retrieved is what was actually downloaded; abstracts_read is what was actually read. Reporting the first as if it were the third overstates the screening by orders of magnitude. If only the first 30 of 256 were retrieved, say so.
provenance.denominators: The surface's provenance keeps four denominators apart for every pass that supports a claim: found (result_count), unique returned (PMIDs actually listed, deduplicated across pages), abstracts obtained, and documents used. A search receipt sees only the first two. Since 1.14.0 the repository MCP also reads by PMID with a receipt (pubmed_fetch_exact): each record delivered whole, pending or as an error, never cut; and scripts/dossier-check.mjs computes the four from the preserved search and reading receipts, the exact final answer and its documented uses, measuring what was preserved, never what was understood. Since 1.15.0 a list screened by title adds a fifth count, kept apart from the four: titles screened (pubmed_summary_exact, reading_and_drilldown.title_screen); it is neither abstracts obtained nor documents used, and dossier-check does not yet read its receipts. Measured 2026-10-17/18: the five behaviour-test cases mixed them, and the coverage of the query, the list delivered, the abstracts obtained and the evidence used diverged.
provenance.exact_query_means_literal: The recorded query is the string that was sent, with the filter expanded inline. A placeholder such as '(topic) AND (<contents of filters/...>)' documents the intent but is not provenance and cannot be re-executed.
provenance.record_at_execution_time: Counters are written when each action happens. Provenance reconstructed from memory at the end of the work is not provenance.
provenance.filter_hash_rule: Record SHA-256 for every filter whose working tree is dirty, mutable, unresolved to a repository commit, or modified for the run; otherwise repository_commit plus filter path is sufficient.
provenance.execution_snapshot_rule: Archive the raw ESearch response or its SHA-256 and the retrieved PMID list or its SHA-256. A reported count alone is not a reproducible execution snapshot.

value_meanings.verified: Checked against the source and found to hold. For query_integrity: PubMed's full diagnostics were read, the sent query was checked for what PubMed ignores silently, and nothing was dropped, broken or doubtful. It is a mechanical statement only: it does not say the query means what the question needs (Automatic Term Mapping, the choice of MeSH and the boolean algebra still need review), nor anything about coverage or reading.
value_meanings.failed: Checked against the source and found NOT to hold. For query_integrity: the diagnostics available, full or partial, show that the query did not run as written (a dropped term, an error, an unusable count, a term missing from querytranslation). Partial diagnostics are enough to reach failed, because one observed anomaly refutes integrity.
value_meanings.unsupported: Cannot be checked with the capabilities at hand. For query_integrity: there are no diagnostics, or only partial ones that show no anomaly. Partial diagnostics can refute integrity but never verify it: measured 2026-10-08, a translation-only engine returned an invented MeSH heading as the same zero as a legitimate one, and echoed the sent query verbatim when every term had been dropped.
value_meanings.why_failed_exists: Until 1.8 a pass whose diagnostics showed a dropped term had no value of its own: calling it unsupported hid a known defect behind an unknown, and nothing else fitted. Measured 2026-10-08 with the reference executor against the repository's real fixtures.

values_by_dimension.rule: Each dimension accepts only the values listed for it. failed exists for a dimension only with its own meaning in failed_by_dimension; extending it to another dimension needs that meaning and its own test, not reuse by analogy.

failed_by_dimension.coverage: A coverage check found relevant records outside the main query in a number or of a kind that can change counts, trends or conclusions. Isolated omissions that cannot change the product are listed under verified instead. Until 1.10 this state had no value, so a corpus missing a third of its subject could only be called planned or unsupported.

operational_status.display_rule: Colours and icons are derived views. Persist semantic values and dimensions, never colour names as the source of truth.
operational_status.unknown_values: A consumer that meets a value it does not know treats it as unsupported, never as verified. Values are added in minor versions (failed in 1.9.0); this rule is what makes that safe.

propose_new_filter_when: the same ad hoc search pattern recurs across multiple questions
an important question type lacks an adequate validated repository filter
existing filters repeatedly produce unacceptable precision or recall for a recurring use case
a high-quality validated external filter can materially improve retrieval
proposal_requirements: include validation reference and metrics when available
test PubMed syntax before proposing repository inclusion
add as candidate before treating as symbolic source of truth

filters.purpose: Identify randomized controlled trials using a high-sensitivity validated strategy.
Identify randomized controlled trials using a validated sensitivity/precision-balanced strategy.

repository_convention.promotion: Move the file to its thematic folder (clinical/, methodology/, scope/, journals/) and replace `# Estado:` with the validation that backs it. While it sits in candidates/, it is not validated.
repository_convention.hard_rule: A candidate must not be used in any search surface, product or flow that produces a clinical recommendation.

filter_repo.development_note: GitHub Pages only serves the default branch. A work branch is not reachable through pages_base_url; during development resolve through raw_base_url with an explicit ref, or through a local checkout.

journal_registry.path_note: journal_filters_data.js is the source of truth and is JavaScript, not JSON. filters/journals/{id}.txt mirrors the same query in plain text for surfaces without a JS parser; if the two ever disagree, the .js wins and the mismatch is reported.

known_mismatches.rule: Declared so that a NEW divergence fails the suite instead of hiding among the old ones. These are to be resolved, not extended.
known_mismatches.measured: 2026-09-15: 71 of 72 ids match. The divergent one lists 19 journals in the .txt and 18 in the .js, with 6 present only in one and 7 only in the other.

sources.filter_catalog: filters/catalog.json, served at filter_catalog.pages_url. The way to discover every filter from a surface that cannot list folders.

degradation.github_unavailable: Stop claims about symbolic filters and request GitHub connection.
degradation.literal_pubmed_unavailable: Do not silently substitute web or semantic search; request a tool capable of literal PubMed execution.
degradation.filter_missing: No suitable curated filter: use ad_hoc_routing, label it as such, and consider proposing a new repository filter.
degradation.router_unavailable: If this router cannot be read but a valid repository filter can, use the filter and declare ad_hoc_routing.

date_window_check.rule: A date window the user did not ask for is a retrieval decision, not part of the question. Before a claim rests on a windowed pass, run the same core without the window in the same unit and check the eligible pearls against it (coverage_check.unit). Pearls that fall outside the window are either kept through the unrestricted pass or the claim is narrowed to the window explicitly, saying what it leaves out. Declaring the window is not enough.
date_window_check.applies_to: Windows of origin agent_policy (provenance.selection_record.fields.date_window), including routing.background.date_policy. A window the user asked for is the scope of the question and is respected; a window embedded in a filter is declared with origin filter.
date_window_check.measured: 2026-10-18, ChatGPT behaviour test, case P (prevalence of childhood obesity in Spain): the agent's own core with 2015:2026[dp] kept 4 of 11 reference studies in 538 records; the same core without the window kept 10 of 11 in 831. The window was declared as a retrieval decision and still cost six studies.
date_window_check.not_a_judgement_of_recency: The check compares coverage. Whether older data still answer the question (a prevalence measured in 2006 is not today's) is judged when reading, after the pearls have been seen.

adaptation.if_pearls_lost_why: Until 1.10 the only trigger to fall back from a specific filter was too few results. A specific filter can return thousands of records and still lose the studies a claim rests on. Measured 2026-10-16 on deprescribing benzodiazepines in older people: Therapy/Narrow returned 3,313 records and lost included intervention studies such as PMID 29492957 and 31523732; nothing in adaptation said to fall back. The trigger is now the loss of eligible pearls (coverage_check.replacing_pass), whatever the count.
adaptation.merge_policy: Deduplicate by PMID and then prioritize relevance, quality, recency and applicability.
adaptation.not_applicable_to: routing.corpus_definition: there, narrowing changes the population instead of making it readable.

tool_requirements.filter_source: GitHub (local checkout, Pages or raw with an explicit ref), or an engine that serves the catalog and the canonical extraction of each filter (the repository MCP: pubmed_filter_catalog and pubmed_get_filter). The second avoids parsing filters by hand on surfaces without code execution.
tool_requirements.rule: A semantic search must not silently substitute a literal PubMed query when reproducibility is required.
tool_requirements.engine_selection: The concrete engine is surface configuration, not a property of this repository. Declare in provenance which engine actually ran each pass.
tool_requirements.semantic_expansion: Optional and always additional; a semantic index may widen the concept space but never replaces a literal PubMed pass when reproducibility is required.
tool_requirements.identifier_retrieval: Retrieval by identifier (full text, formatted citations, related articles, preprints, ID conversion) is a different capability from search. An engine may be adopted for it without being trusted for search passes, and the reverse. Its output feeds reading_and_drilldown, never coverage: a related-articles list is a discovery lane, not a search pass; extracted full text is checked against the record it claims to be (title and DOI or PMID) before it is read as that article; and the provider that actually answered is recorded, because a fallback chain changes the source without changing the tool name.
tool_requirements.mesh_lookup_tools: A tool that looks headings up in db=mesh is discovery under query_execution_contract.rule_for_headings, not validation, whatever its name promises.

surface_profiles.rule: A section requiring a capability the surface does not have is skipped explicitly and said out loud, never simulated.

query_builder_surface.description: A surface that composes and hands over a query; it does not execute, read or merge.

conversational_surface_with_literal_pubm.description: A surface able to execute exact PubMed syntax, read PubMed's own diagnostics for every pass, carry long composed queries and read abstracts.

conversational_surface_with_unverifiable.description: A surface whose engine executes exact PubMed syntax but does not return querytranslation, warninglist and errorlist as PubMed sent them. It returns real records; it cannot show what PubMed executed. Transport is judged separately, per request.
forbidden: reporting a count as a verified search result
counting a pass as coverage for a report, decision, publication or review
recording a tool's echo, applied-filter list or notice as querytranslation or warninglist
conversational_surface_with_unverifiable.still_allowed: Records it returns may support a claim once each one is read and checked against its PubMed record; what they cannot support is a statement about how much was searched.
conversational_surface_with_unverifiable.handoff: When a result will support a claim about coverage, say that this surface cannot verify its execution and hand the query to an engine with execution_diagnostics. Retrieval by identifier stays available under tool_requirements.identifier_retrieval.

conversational_surface_without_literal_p.description: A conversational surface with web access but no exact PubMed execution.
forbidden: presenting semantic search output as a PubMed pass

surface_profiles.per_engine_and_pass: Profiles describe engines, not products. A surface with several engines is profiled per pass, by the engine that ran it. long_query_transport is judged per request: an engine that returns full diagnostics but cannot carry a long composed query still verifies the passes it carries whole, and declares a transport failure for the rest; a transport limit is not a missing diagnostic. A platform is not bound to a profile forever: an engine it connects later is profiled by what that engine returns.
